# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–34 (Updated 2026-10-13)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Summer of ninth year after Waterloo (1830). Chapter 33 spans Sunday, 26th April through following week; Chapter 34 begins summer. Chapter 33 Sunday includes house dinner at 8 PM with five or six men; gambling afterward, card-room convenes ~11 PM Sunday night.
- **Key Locations**: London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Abchurch Lane, Beargarden Club, Langham Hotel, Euston Square Railway Station, Bruton Street, Lincoln's Inn, Queen's Gate); Coventry Island; Queen's Crawley; Coldcombe and Mirecombe farms; Bryngate; Pumpernickel; Ostend; Hampshire ("the Evergreens"); Brussels; Aix-la-Chapelle; Bath and Cheltenham; Carbury Hall; Carbury Chase; Caversham; Sussex; Quenwick; Dunholt village; Salford; Sheepstone; Bungay; Sheep's Acre Farm; Sheepstone Birches; Yarlton; Staveton; Fenmere hill farms; Suffolk.

## Major Deaths
- **John Sedley, Mr. Osborne, Joseph Sedley, Colonel Rawdon Crawley, Sir Pitt**: All deceased as previously documented.

## Rebecca's Arc
- Never became Lady Crawley; styles herself so. Son (Sir Rawdon, young baronet) receives liberal allowance but declines to see her. Appears very wealthy at Bath and Cheltenham. Busies herself in piety and Charity Lists.

## Amelia and William Dobbin
- Married at Dike (Ostend); Amelia initiated encounter in "dripping white bonnet and shawl." Dobbin quit service, rented "the Evergreens" (Hampshire). Devoted father; fonder of daughter Jane than of his History of the Punjaub.

## Lady Carbury and Family

**Lady Carbury**: Lives on Welbeck Street with Felix and Henrietta. Authored "Criminal Queens." Crushed by "Evening Pulpit" review by Mr. Jones (Mr. Alf's reviewer); praised by "Morning Breakfast Table" review by Mr. Broune. Suspects Alf orders hostile reviews of friends' works. Proposed scheme: if Henrietta married Roger, Felix could inherit his name, title, property. Felix consented to remain at Manor House. At Monday Caversham dinner, found Melmotte "heavy on her hands." Urged Felix to formally propose to Marie's father, warning: "don't put it off; you don't know how many slips there may be between the cup and the lip." Felix refused, claiming awkwardness.

**Felix Carbury**: Beautiful; cynosure of mother's eyes. Won £2,000 from Lord Grasslough, £400 from Miles Grendall at gaming. Director of South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Company. **Sunday, 26th April: Found Madame Melmotte, Marie, Georgiana Longestaffe, and Lord Nidderdale in drawing-room. Marie fell asleep; secretly instructed Felix to find Melmotte in book-room below. Felix descended, found Melmotte waking with cigar; Melmotte assumed Felix came about railway shares and resolved to be stern. Melmotte's strategy: intimidate through assumed superiority, relying on timidity/ignorance of colleagues, or cultivate their cupidity; prefers young associates as more timid and less greedy. Felix wished himself at Beargarden. When Melmotte questioned his income, Felix lacked courage to speak truth. Melmotte, puzzled by English peerage system, questioned how baronet could be heir to Esquire. Felix walked to club afterward feeling checkmated, full of wrath, unable to stand against Melmotte, whom he deemed greatest brute ever created.** **After house dinner Sunday night (7 PM), Felix approached Dolly Longestaffe for cash, urgently needing to "take up a lot of shares in the city to-morrow; or perhaps Wednesday might do." Claimed Melmotte said only objection to him and Marie's marriage was money; must appear to have funds.** **In smoking-room, Felix attempted business with Miles Grendall (Secretary), beginning with unusual courtesy, believing Grendall had influence with share distributor. When Grendall remained impassive, Felix grew angry, demanding in whisper: "Then, when the deuce will you pay me what you owe me?" Asked how much Grendall owed; countenance showed plainly he was speaking in anger. Grendall made no answer.** **Sunday night card-room (~11 PM): Felix doubted propriety of joining party with man seeming liberated from obligation to pay, but needed gambling table. Party began with whist but switched to loo at Grendall's persistence, despite objections from Grasslough, Dolly, Felix, and Nidderdale. During play, Felix sat next to Grendall, observed him moving chair away and toward Dolly. Felix became moderate in play, tossing cards, almost always losing, losing minimum, watching board. Grendall won heavily, particularly from Paul Montague. Grasslough remarked on Grendall's run of luck; Grendall countered that he'd lost so much before, and had destroyed paper counters representing £1,000+ while receiving considerable ready money—"quite a godsend to him."**

**Sheepstone Meeting (Sunday, 19th April)**: Met Ruby Ruggles; promised to see her again Tuesday morning at kitchen garden bottom. Resolved not to keep promise; planned to write asking her to come to London.

**Henrietta Carbury**: Rejected Roger's suit, claiming too young and age disparity insurmountable. Within week, Paul returned "as a still dear friend," promising not to see her three months. Wore rose from Roger's room. When met Roger at door, there was "more in her eyes of graciousness towards him than he had ever seen there before." Roger declared love anew (Chapter 32 evening); Henrietta has not committed; Roger's determination remains unshaken.

## Ruby Ruggles
- Granddaughter of old Daniel Ruggles, of Sheep's Acre, parish of Sheepstone, near Bungay. Pretty with long glossy ringlets, large round dark eyes, clear dark complexion; strong, healthy, tall; possessed own will. Had been to marry John Crumb (marriage abandoned/postponed). Understood degradation must be avoided. After Sunday meeting with Felix, resolved: "I suppose I am to be his wedded wife...I'll never be nothing unless I'm that."

## The Melmottes

**Augustus Melmotte**: Chairman of South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Company. Arrived London from Paris within two years; claims English birth but speaks with accent betraying "long expatriation." Big man with large whiskers, rough hair; expression of mental power on harsh vulgar face. In City, his name "worth any money." Taken up old Longestaffe's affairs; has Caversham and Sussex property. Miles Grendall serves as usher/secretary. **By Chapter 33 Board day, has twice sold fifty shares at £112 10s., receiving cheques for £625 each (£25 profit per share above £100 nominal). During Whitsun week country visit, remained in summer-house with Lord Alfred, smoking, drinking brandy and seltzer, appearing not in good humour.**

**Marie Melmotte**: Speaks English well; has begun forming own opinions. Rejected Lord Grasslough; has experience with Lord Nidderdale. Currently pursued by Sir Felix Carbury (claimed favourite in London). **Sunday: Fell asleep in chair before fire caught. Secretly instructed Felix to find father in book-room, telling him "Papa is down-stairs in the book-room. Lord Alfred was told when he came that he was out." Resolved on constancy toward Felix; rejected other suitors. Felt complete happiness; promised to tell mother. Blushes when Felix mentioned, fearing his faithlessness.** **[Letter from Marie to Felix, date unspecified]: "I heard your note;—such a scrap! Of course papa would talk about money because he never thinks of anything else. I don't know anything about money, and I don't care in the least how much you have got. Papa has got plenty, and I think he would give us some if we were once married. I have told mamma, but mamma is always afraid of everything. Papa is very cross to her sometimes;—more so than to me. I will try to tell him, though I can't always get at him. I very often hardly see him all day long. But I don't mean to be afraid of him, and will tell him that on my word and honour I will never marry any one except you. I don't think he will beat me, but if he does, I'll bear it,—for your sake. He does beat mamma sometimes, I know."**

**Madame Melmotte**: Gracious as usual but never very gracious. Called Miss Longestaffe "a great bore" and "fatigante." Dismissed Marie's declarations of caring. Appears to know of Felix's offer; does not absolutely disapprove.

## The Longestaffes

**Sir Merton Longestaffe**: Determined no more London expenses that year; family will not return from Caversham. Desires to sell Pickering and disembarrass Caversham from debt. Dolly refused to consent unless half produce given to him. Broke promise to Georgiana of returning to London.

**Georgiana Longestaffe**: Made strong protest against Melmottes; threatened to stay in London. Father refused; she felt "treachery." Meditated revenge: "I will do something. I'm not going to be cheated and swindled." Most angered that family "should have condescended to be civil to the Melmottes down in the country." Following morning, Lady Pomona handed her undated invitation from Melmotte to stay with them. Breathed very hard; noted insolence. Questioned mother. Expressed contempt for Melmottes, calling them vulgar. Yet concluded: "I'll go." **Friday morning before departure to railway station, conversation with younger sister Sophia was "almost touching." Georgiana failed to hold up her head as usual; cowed. Told Sophia: "Sophy, I do so envy you staying here."** **By Sunday, present at Grosvenor Square drawing-room with Madame Melmotte, Marie, and Lord Nidderdale, carrying on flirtation with Nidderdale in half whisper, wholly indifferent to hostess or young lady of house. Nidderdale said "We know what brings you here."**

**Sophia Longestaffe**: Younger Miss. Somewhat reconciled to country sojourn as it inflicted fitting punishment on Georgiana and because Mr. Whitstable's proximity made difference.

**Adolphus (Dolly) Longestaffe**: Has own rooms in Bruton Street; seldom dines with family. Obdurate regarding his own rights in property dealings. Sunday evening sauntered into Beargarden at ~7 PM seeking sherry and bitters; present at house dinner and card-room gambling.

**Lady Pomona**: Complained of headache at Caversham; slept through afternoon's tension.

## South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Scheme

**The Enterprise**: Railway from Salt Lake City, branching from San Francisco and Chicago line, passing through New Mexico and Arizona into Mexico, terminating at Vera Cruz. Approximately 2,000 miles. Fisker considers cost questions "beside the mark and childish." Concession obtained from United States Government.

**Financial Strategy**: Stock at par; shares sold at premium to "run them up even to 110," yielding three hundred thousand dollars minimum. Directors understood fortune made by floating shares, not making actual railway.

**London Directorate**: Melmotte (chairman), Lord Alfred Grendall, Sir Felix Carbury, Samuel Cohenlupe (MP for Staines), Lord Nidderdale, Paul Montague.

**Fisker's Departure**: Started Saturday morning, 19th April. Met by Nidderdale and Montague.

## Paul Montague
Living at Beargarden. Junior member of firm; English. Personally dislikes Fisker but unable to resist his combination. Trembles for his money. Entertained Lord Alfred once; dined twice with Melmotte in Grosvenor Square. Saw good deal of Sir Felix, Lord Nidderdale; champagne consumption increased. Could not wake up on London mornings with satisfactory thoughts as at Carbury Hall. At Beargarden cardroom, offered to undertake Grendall's debt himself; disallowed. **Sunday night card-room: Present at gambling; won heavily from him by Grendall in run of luck.**

## Lord Nidderdale
Intent on marrying Marie Melmotte for her fortune. Claims not afraid of Melmotte, believing Melmotte "rather likes me, because I've always been on the square with him," asserting "If it depended on him, you know, I should have the girl to-morrow." On Friday Board day, walked with Melmotte to Abchurch Lane offices, asking about his position regarding shares. Melmotte told him to wait, shares would be allocated but not transferable until he qualifies by investing "a few thousand pounds." **Sunday drawing-room: Flirting with Miss Longestaffe in half whisper, wholly indifferent to hostess or young lady of house. Sunday night: Present at card-room gambling; objected to loo but capitulated.**

## Roger Carbury
Nearly forty years old. Never owed shilling he could not pay; father likewise. Firmly opposed to Melmotte connection on principle; holds old-fashioned idea that "touching of pitch will defile." Took degree at Oxford; became "pervert," supposed "convert." Works as priest earning day-labourer's wages; forced to buy second-hand clothes. Soft heart; knows Lady Carbury false and Felix worthless, yet condemns himself for harsh words. During Sunday evening with Father Barham, engaged in theological debate; became tired of priest's intolerance. Later showed courtesy as host despite disapproval of Melmotte scheme. Declared love to Henrietta anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination remains unshaken.

## Father John Barham
Priest of Beccles. Dogmatic Catholic; believes man should abandon reason to care of another or others. Faith sufficient unto itself. In county only twelve months; knew nearly every Roman Catholic's name within borders.

## Property Relations
**Daniel Ruggles' Land**: Holds Sheep's Acre Farm on bishop's lease, part of property which belonged to bishopric of Elmham. Also holds small extent of outlying meadow belonging to Carbury estate; thus one of Roger Carbury's tenants. Sheepstone Birches (wood/copse) belonged to Roger.

## Other Characters
- **Miles Grendall**: Secretary/usher to Melmotte. Does not pay debts of honour; made no answer regarding repayment; lacks impudence to avoid discussing business while accepting that private matters separate from affairs of business. **Sunday card-room: Won heavily, particularly from Paul Montague; destroyed paper counters representing £1,000+; received considerable ready money "quite a godsend to him." When pressed by Felix about debt, rose and suggested billiards, walking slowly out of room, leaving Felix to take what revenge he pleased. Felix feared Grendall was more popular man than himself and did not expose transaction to whole room.** **During hour of play, observed moving chair farther from Felix and nearer to Dolly.**
- **Lord Grasslough**: Present at Sunday card-room gambling.
- **Cotho Hollwood, Thidrek Corrett, Nynelle, Nydan, Elnar**: Characters appearing in scenic/descriptive passages; uncertain narrative status (possibly background figures or names introduced without plot connection).
